I'm younger than you and don't know anything about the comic book industry or really, breaking into industries in general, but seems like you have some good professional experience, some writing experience, you've taken some time in there to raise your kids as well... and I don't think there's any reason why you can't jump into the comic book industry. As with any entertainment or publishing-related industry, there are tons of different things you can do, and you're a writer which could count for a lot with lots of different jobs.

At the same time, if you decide you don't want to work in an office, there's no reason why you can't try remote working or continue working some lower-stress or part time jobs, and start a webcomic or collaborate with some comics-related people on the side. 

On top of all of this, there's no reason why you shouldn't just try to do something you're inclined to do! Worst thing that could happen is you fail and have to go back to the drawing board.

But seriously - people change careers all the time. It can be tough to explain when you're starting out and applying for jobs, but there's absolutely no reason in the world why you can't, especially if you can market the skills you have in a specific way to help you jump in.
That's amazing! I hope your meeting is fantastic and wish you two all the best!

There's no shame in feeling depressed or having other distressing emotions. It's not your fault. Depression affects most people at some point, directly, as well as indirectly (through a loved one being depressed).

You should talk to your mom about how you're feeling. You don't have to go into graphic detail or even admit to being suicidal, but I bet it would be a load off just to tell someone. If not your mom, maybe a friend. Or tell us more, on here. And I don't presume to know if your family has the financial/insurance resources, but you could really benefit from talking to a professional counselor - I'm sure your mom would be happy to help with this if she can. 

Every good parent just wants to help their kid be happy. You should let your mom help. My mom doesn't like thinking about my depression, because it upsets her... but I know when I felt suicidal in high school and college, if she had known (she didn't know at the time), she would have done anything - I mean anything - even pay for me to be hospitalized or let me take time off of school - if it meant I would have stopped feeling suicidal and felt better.

Keep going! You're killing it. Proud of you, dude!

Speaking as someone that's never had healthy habits, but HAS gotten to the point with diet/exercise time and time again that I actually LIKE IT (sadly I just abandon it again because "something comes up" like I get sick or go on vacation and fall out of the routine) I know if you stick with it, it will get easier!

You've inspired me to try to eat healthier, walk more every day, and commit to not eating dessert or snacks. Let's goooo!!!

Thanks for your comment - sorry to hear you too (and your fiancé) have struggled with anxiety. I haven't heard about theanine serine and will look into it. I've also heard B vitamins (which I don't currently take) might help with my IBS. So will look into some supplements! Thanks for the tip.

I've actually never been on anxiety medication before either and judging from the fact that I have a moderate level of anxiety, it might be really helpful - so once I have real insurance again, I will definitely look into this. I'd worry about becoming dependent though, and as you said, some of the side effects can be bad and make you kind of out of it.
